explanation: The exact statement `Antitone (· ≤ x)` for `[Preorder α]` exists only once in Mathlib, namely as the target theorem itself (`Mathlib/Order/BoundedOrder/Monotone.lean:75`); Batteries and Lean core contain no `Antitone`/`Monotone` order lemmas at all. Searches for the natural naming variants (`monotone_le`, `antitone_le`, `monotone_ge`, `antitone_ge`, `monotone_lt`, `antitone_lt`, `antitone_const_iff`, `_dual`/`to_dual`-generated forms) turn up only the sibling lemmas in the same file, and a content search (`Antitone (fun … ≤ …)`, `Antitone (· ∈ …)`, `: Antitone (· …)`) finds no other declaration with this shape. The closest relatives are: `monotone_le : Monotone (x ≤ ·)` (the order-dual statement, not the same result — transferring it needs the extra bridge `antitone_comp_ofDual_iff`/`Monotone.dual_left` and a reindexing of the type to `αᵒᵈ`), `Set.antitone_mem : Antitone (· ∈ s) ↔ IsLowerSet s` and `isLowerSet_setOfPred : IsLowerSet {a | p a} ↔ Antitone p` (general biconditional characterizations of antitone predicates by lower sets; deriving the target from them needs the auxiliary fact `IsLowerSet.Iic`, whose own proof is essentially `le_trans`), and `IsLowerSet.Iic : IsLowerSet (Iic x)` (a statement about sets, only related to the target by unfolding `Antitone`, `IsLowerSet` and `Set.Iic`). None of these carries the theorem's result as stated, so no duplicate was found.
